construct: During fasting, fatty-acid oxidation and hormonal/transcriptional signals increase PDK4 activity/expression. PDKs phosphorylate and inactivate the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, decreasing pyruvate oxidation and conserving three-carbon substrates such as pyruvate, lactate, and alanine for gluconeogenesis.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Fasting raises PDK4 and fatty-acid-derived signals; PDK phosphorylation inactivates PDH and preserves three-carbon substrates for gluconeogenesis.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: PDH phosphatase is a direct regulator of the same complex, but it dephosphorylates and activates PDH, opposite the observed fasting response.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The direction of PDH activity and fasting fuel selection uniquely require increased PDK-mediated inhibitory phosphorylation.
